checks.check: Explains that the mutation score, the property-test generators and/or the pairwise coverage measure the port against itself, so they cannot reveal legacy rules the port lacks
checks.evidence: plan.md section 1: "Every adequacy measure we report comes from the port itself" ... "None of these measures can see a rule the port lacks", naming mutants, pairwise factors and rapid properties.

checks.check: Works out from comparator.yaml at least two concrete differences the parity suite cannot see (line order, null versus absent, number scale or notation, error message text) and proposes a way to ask around them
checks.evidence: plan.md section 1 names all four ("arrays: sort hides the order of response lines", "nulls: drop merges null with an absent field", 12.5/12.50/1.25E+1, error.message); F1 re-diffs stored raw responses with each normalization disabled and round 10 records raw bodies.

checks.check: Treats the decisions sourced from the design doc (D3, D12, D15, D22) as unverified against legacy and gives them requests
checks.evidence: plan.md decision audit marks D3, D12, D15, D22 as "guess"; requests E1-E4 (D3), G2-G4 (D12), V2-V3 (D15), V1 (D22).

checks.check: Treats a hand-written exception list (D7 rounding categories or D21 jurisdictions) as a possible footprint of a general rule and proposes requests that tell the rule from the list
checks.evidence: plan.md section 3: "Both are typical footprints of an unknown general mechanism"; D7 double-vs-BigDecimal table with R1-R8, D21 candidates (a)-(d) separated by Z1-Z6.

checks.check: Includes structural relations over rule uploads: reordering rules or groups, adding an irrelevant rule, duplicating, or splitting a rule
checks.evidence: plan.md: ZZ-T2 uploads zeta, alpha, mid and ZZ-T3 "in reverse" (E1-E4); ZZ-T4 duplicates a rule name (E5-E6); E7 re-uploads without alpha.

checks.check: Asks what happens on an identity collision (two rules or groups with the same name, a reused name across jurisdictions)
checks.evidence: plan.md: "ZZ-T4: two rules both named dup"; E5 "rejected versus accepted", E6 "first wins / last wins / both apply".

checks.check: Uses the legacy platform (Java, Jackson, PostgreSQL) to propose concrete hypotheses (e.g. trim semantics, BigDecimal scale, Jackson coercion, column length limits)
checks.evidence: plan.md: "String.trim() (strips <= U+0020, not NBSP)" vs Go TrimSpace, PostgreSQL row order without ORDER BY, Jackson int binding truncating 2.5, BigDecimal keeping 12.50 / printing 1.25E+1.

checks.check: Proposes field state or spelling variants (absent / null / empty / blank, or number spellings) for at least one input field
checks.evidence: plan.md G2: exemptionCode as EX, lowercase, " EX ", "EX\t", "", null; N1 unitPrice 1.25E1, "1.25E1", "0012.50"; Z9 quantity null.

checks.check: The round is at most 50 requests, tiered or ordered so that a budget cut drops the least informative requests first
checks.evidence: plan.md request table counts exactly 50 rows, tiered M/S/Y, with "Drop order if the budget is cut: Remove from the bottom up: V3, V2, V1, P1 ...".

checks.check: Brackets the round with control replays of already-answered requests to detect drift, and asks to record the legacy build or version
checks.evidence: plan.md: K2/K3 replay goldens r8-33 and r9-21 at the start and K4/K5 at the end; K1/K6 GET the build or version endpoint; F3 asks whether the stand runs the production build.

checks.check: Keeps the shared stand safe: rule uploads go to jurisdictions no recorded answer or other team depends on, or existing configuration is exported and restored
checks.evidence: plan.md ground rules: "Every probe that changes configuration goes to a new jurisdiction in the ZZ-* namespace ... Probes against real jurisdictions are quotes only", with an export-and-restore fallback.

checks.check: Labels unverified expectations about legacy as hypotheses rather than stating them as fact
checks.evidence: plan.md section 2: "Live alternatives are hypotheses"; F3 "treat the answers as hypotheses until a probe confirms them"; section 6 forbids recording a mechanism until the separating request is answered.
